votes.evidence: Read bc7090d:src/rules/engine.ts runRules lines 215-227: when rule.check throws, the catch block runs `if (applies) rulesRun++`, pushes an INTERNAL finding with severity 'info' and platforms ['spec'] into `findings` only (not `scored`), then `continue`s. Nothing is added to `skipped`, and snap.coverage is left alone. No guard exists elsewhere. `git grep INTERNAL -- src` finds it only in sarif.ts (a rule entry) and a comment in junit.ts. buildReport (src/report/index.ts:45-71) sets complete = coverage.toolLevel==='ok' and verdicts from the error/warning counts only. It computes the score from result.scored, and failed from the gate plus fatal/stopped/incompleteFails, so an INTERNAL finding affects none of them. The CLI exit code (cli.ts:835) is built from these same values. The existing tests (engine.test.ts:29, remediation-wp9-report-redact.test.ts:150) only check that the info finding is emitted, which matches the current behaviour and does not catch the gap. Ran a minimal vitest in a detached worktree at bc7090d: one rule with error severity on all platforms that returns a finding gives {rulesRun:1, scored:1, failed:true, score:88, verdicts BLOCKED, cov ok}. The same rule ID throwing instead gives {rulesRun:1, scored:0, failed:false, score:100, verdicts 'NO AUTOMATED BLOCKERS', cov ok}, so a crash turns FAIL into PASS (exit 0). This goes against the project's rule that a check missing data is partial and never a pass, which the engine already applies to stops (STOPPED_REASON) and connect failures (CONNECT_REASON). I did not re-run the reported 59-rule toString-object case: whether real input reaches a throwing rule depends on A13-01 or on a future rule bug. That is why I rate it medium and not high. Worktree removed.
